cards.back: feudal society (a system where land and power belong to a small ruling class)
cards.example: 清朝是中国封建社会最后一个朝代。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Qing Dynasty was the last dynasty of China's feudal society.
cards.breakdown: 封：土堆（土）上种树（寸），表示封土封地 · 建：用笔（聿）踏出脚步（廴），开创建立 · 社：土地神（示）的聚会（土），人们聚集的组织 · 会：人们聚在一起，合在一处

cards.back: territory / domain (all the land within a country's borders)
cards.example: 清朝初期疆域达到1,200万平方千米。
cards.exampleTranslation: In its early period, the Qing Dynasty's territory reached 12 million square kilometers.
cards.breakdown: 疆：弓（弓）划定土地（田）边界，极其宽广 · 域：围起来的（口）土地（土），加上武力（戈）守护

cards.back: Celestial Empire (China's self-important title — arrogant belief in its own superiority)
cards.example: 大清以天朝上国自居，不知道世界正在发生巨大变化。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Qing considered itself the Celestial Empire, unaware of the great changes happening in the world.
cards.breakdown: 天：人头顶上那片广阔的天空 · 朝：早晨太阳升起，臣民朝见君王 · 上：基准线上方，表示高级、上等 · 国：有边界的土地，守护着领土

cards.back: isolationism / closed-door policy (shut the gates and guard oneself — refusing contact with the outside world)
cards.example: 大清闭关自守，使中国落后于世界的先进潮流。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Qing's closed-door policy caused China to fall behind the world's advanced trends.
cards.breakdown: 闭：门（门）关闭，不让外人进入 · 关：门栓拉上，关起来 · 自：鼻子的象形，表示自己 · 守：屋顶（宀）下用手（寸）看守

cards.back: blind arrogance (overconfident and ignoring reality — literally 'blind eyes, puffed up self')
cards.example: 清朝盲目自大，不知道欧洲正在发生巨大变化。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Qing was blindly arrogant, unaware of the great changes happening in Europe.
cards.breakdown: 盲：眼睛（目）死了（亡），什么也看不见 · 目：眼睛的象形 · 自：表示自己 · 大：人张开双臂，非常大、伟大

cards.back: trade deficit (importing more than you export — money flows out) ↔ 顺差
cards.example: 在中英贸易中，英国一直有很大的逆差。
cards.exampleTranslation: In China-Britain trade, Britain always had a large trade deficit.
cards.breakdown: 逆：人倒着走（辶），违反顺序，反向的 · 差：差额，这里指贸易的差额

cards.back: woollen goods (woven woollen cloth — a British export that failed to sell in China)
cards.example: 英国的呢绒、钟表等在中国销路不好。
cards.exampleTranslation: British woollen goods and clocks did not sell well in China.
cards.breakdown: 呢：口（口）中带着毛料的质感，指粗毛织物 · 绒：丝线（纟）做成的绒布，软而厚实

cards.back: Industrial Revolution (18th–19th c. shift from farming to factory production, starting in Europe)
cards.example: 欧洲的工业革命带来了全新的生产方式和社会变化。
cards.exampleTranslation: Europe's Industrial Revolution brought entirely new methods of production and social change.
cards.breakdown: 工：像一把尺子，表示工作与技艺 · 业：一排排竖立，表示一项事业 · 革：动物的皮，后来表示根本改变 · 命：跪下听令，天命、生命

cards.back: opium (highly addictive drug smuggled into China by British traders)
cards.example: 英国开始了罪恶的鸦片贸易，每年有四万多箱鸦片卖到中国。
cards.exampleTranslation: Britain began the evil opium trade, with over 40,000 chests of opium sold to China each year.
cards.breakdown: 鸦：黑色的乌鸦（鸟），发出yā的叫声 · 片：木头切开的一半，薄薄的一片

cards.back: ban on opium / prohibit opium-smoking (禁烟 = 禁止鸦片)
cards.example: 清朝皇帝命令林则徐到广州禁烟。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Qing emperor ordered Lin Zexu to go to Guangzhou to ban opium.
cards.breakdown: 禁：两棵树（林），森林神圣不可侵犯，加上示（示），表示禁止 · 烟：火（火）燃烧产生的烟雾（因）

cards.back: to destroy completely by burning / to incinerate
cards.example: 林则徐在虎门将收来的鸦片全部销毁。
cards.exampleTranslation: Lin Zexu completely destroyed all the collected opium at Humen.
cards.breakdown: 销：金属（钅）被火融化消除（肖） · 毁：臼（臼）与工（工）结合，表示砸烂、彻底破坏

cards.back: warship / armed naval vessel
cards.example: 1840年，英国派军舰入侵中国广州和浙江。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1840, Britain sent warships to invade Guangzhou and Zhejiang in China.
cards.breakdown: 军：战车（车）被覆盖保护，是军队的意思 · 舰：船（舟）加上观察（监），是大型战船

cards.back: Humen Opium Burning — Lin Zexu's 1839 destruction of 20,000+ chests of British opium at Humen, near Guangzhou
cards.example: 林则徐在虎门将鸦片全部销毁，这就是历史上著名的"虎门销烟"。
cards.exampleTranslation: Lin Zexu destroyed all the opium at Humen — this is the famous 'Humen Opium Burning' in history.

cards.back: Opium War (1840–1842) — Britain invaded China after Lin Zexu destroyed British opium; China was defeated
cards.example: 1840年，英国发动了"鸦片战争"，清军奋力抵抗，但最终战败。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1840, Britain launched the Opium War; the Qing army fought hard but ultimately lost.

cards.back: to sign / conclude (a treaty or agreement)
cards.example: 1842年，清政府被迫同英国签订了《南京条约》。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1842, the Qing government was forced to sign the Treaty of Nanjing with Britain.
cards.breakdown: 签：竹（竹）制的笔，用来书写签名（佥）· 订：用言语（讠）钉（丁）定，约好不变

cards.back: treaty / convention (a formal written agreement between countries)
cards.example: 《南京条约》是中国近代史上第一个不平等条约。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Treaty of Nanjing was the first unequal treaty in modern Chinese history.
cards.breakdown: 条：细长的一根，表示一条一条的规定 · 约：用丝线（纟）捆绑约束，做出承诺

cards.back: unequal treaty (a treaty imposed by a stronger nation on a weaker one by force)
cards.example: 一连串的不平等条约使中国丧失了大量土地和财富。
cards.exampleTranslation: A series of unequal treaties caused China to lose vast amounts of land and wealth.
cards.breakdown: 不平等：不公平，一方受益另一方受损 · 条约：两国之间正式签订的协议

cards.back: war indemnity / to pay reparations (money a defeated nation is forced to pay)
cards.example: 条约规定中国向英国赔款2,100万银圆。
cards.exampleTranslation: The treaty stipulated that China pay Britain an indemnity of 21 million silver dollars.
cards.breakdown: 赔：用钱财（贝）补偿对方的损失 · 款：流动的钱财，这里指赔偿的金额

cards.back: to cede (give up territory to another country by force of treaty)
cards.example: 《南京条约》规定中国割让香港岛给英国。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Treaty of Nanjing stipulated that China cede Hong Kong Island to Britain.
cards.breakdown: 割：用刀（刀）切断分开（害）· 让：用言语（讠）退步，把东西让给别人

cards.back: colony (a territory fully controlled and exploited by a foreign power)
cards.example: 鸦片战争之前，中国还不是殖民地。
cards.exampleTranslation: Before the Opium War, China was not yet a colony.
cards.breakdown: 殖：像植物（植）一样在外地繁殖扎根 · 民：古代被统治的人民 · 地：大地，土地

cards.back: semi-colony (partly colonized — sovereignty weakened but not fully lost, as happened to China)
cards.example: 1840年鸦片战争后，中国变为半殖民地半封建社会。
cards.exampleTranslation: After the 1840 Opium War, China became a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society.
cards.breakdown: 半：把东西分成两半，表示不完全 · 殖民地：被外国控制的土地

cards.back: to lose / forfeit (something important — land, rights, or power)
cards.example: 一连串的不平等条约使中国丧失了150万平方千米的土地。
cards.exampleTranslation: A series of unequal treaties caused China to forfeit 1.5 million square kilometers of land.
cards.breakdown: 丧：死亡、失去，古代像送葬的仪式 · 失：手里（手）的东西滑落，失去了

cards.back: to overthrow / topple (a government or ruler)
cards.example: 辛亥革命推翻了清朝的统治，结束了封建帝制。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Revolution of 1911 overthrew Qing rule, ending the feudal imperial system.
cards.breakdown: 推：用手（扌）向前推出去 · 翻：用翅膀（羽）翻转，倒过来

cards.back: the Revolution of 1911 — led by Sun Yat-sen, overthrew the Qing Dynasty and established the Republic of China
cards.example: 1911年孙中山领导的辛亥革命推翻了满清，建立了民国。
cards.exampleTranslation: The 1911 Revolution led by Sun Yat-sen overthrew the Manchu Qing and established the Republic of China.
cards.breakdown: 辛亥：1911年的干支纪年（辛亥年）· 革命：彻底的政治变革，推翻旧政权

cards.back: provisional / temporary (for a limited period, not yet permanent)
cards.example: 1912年孙中山宣布成立中华民国临时政府。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1912, Sun Yat-sen declared the establishment of the provisional government of the Republic of China.
cards.breakdown: 临：人（人）俯视（品）某处，接近某个时刻或地点 · 时：日（日）加上寸（一点时间），时间、时机

cards.back: to declare / announce officially (a public, formal announcement)
cards.example: 孙中山宣布中华民国临时政府在南京成立。
cards.exampleTranslation: Sun Yat-sen declared the establishment of the provisional government of the Republic of China in Nanjing.
cards.breakdown: 宣：屋顶（宀）下面向外传播（亘），公开宣告 · 布：用手把织好的布料摊开，铺展公告

cards.back: Qing Dynasty (1644–1912) — last imperial dynasty of China, founded by the Manchu people, capital Beijing
cards.example: 清朝是中国封建社会最后一个朝代，由满族人建立。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Qing Dynasty was the last dynasty of China's feudal society, founded by the Manchu people.

cards.back: Manchu people — ethnic group from northeast China who conquered the Ming and founded the Qing Dynasty in 1644
cards.example: 满族人建立了清朝，1644年入山海关打败了李自成。
cards.exampleTranslation: The Manchu people founded the Qing Dynasty, entering Shanhai Pass in 1644 and defeating Li Zicheng.

cards.back: Emperor Kangxi (r. 1661–1722) — one of China's greatest emperors; unified Taiwan in 1683; Qing reached its peak under his rule
cards.example: 1683年康熙皇帝出兵统一了台湾。
cards.exampleTranslation: In 1683, Emperor Kangxi sent troops to unify Taiwan.

cards.back: Lin Zexu (1785–1850) — Qing official who destroyed British opium at Humen in 1839; hero of the anti-opium movement
cards.example: 林则徐到广州禁烟，在虎门将鸦片全部销毁。
cards.exampleTranslation: Lin Zexu went to Guangzhou to ban opium and destroyed it all at Humen.

cards.back: Empress Dowager Cixi (1835–1908) — de facto ruler of late Qing; conservative, executed Hundred Days' Reform leaders, failed to resist foreign invasion
cards.example: 西太后顽固守旧，杀害了百日维新的谭嗣同等人。
cards.exampleTranslation: Empress Dowager Cixi was stubbornly conservative and killed Tan Sitong and others who supported the Hundred Days' Reform.

cards.back: Tan Sitong (1865–1898) — reformer executed by Empress Dowager Cixi after the failure of the Hundred Days' Reform
cards.example: 谭嗣同是百日维新的改革者，被西太后杀害。
cards.exampleTranslation: Tan Sitong was a reformer of the Hundred Days' Reform who was executed by Empress Dowager Cixi.

cards.back: Sun Yat-sen (1866–1925) — leader of the Revolution of 1911, founded the Republic of China, known as the 'Father of the Nation'
cards.example: 孙中山领导辛亥革命，推翻满清，建立中华民国。
cards.exampleTranslation: Sun Yat-sen led the Revolution of 1911, overthrew the Manchu Qing, and established the Republic of China.
